basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 3.' and it opens '(Cap. XXXVII.—Vers. 3.) Et Israel dilexit Joseph super omnes filios suos, quia erat'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Cap. XXXVII.—Vers. 3.) Et Israel dilexit Joseph super omnes filios suos, quia erat filius senectutis: et fecit ei tunicam variam. Pro varia tunica, Aquila interpretatus est tunicam ἀστραγάλειον, id est, tunicam talarem. Symmachus, tunicam manicatam, sive quod ad talos usque descenderet, et manibus artificis mira esset varietate distincta: sive quod haberet manicas: Antiqui enim magis colobiis utebantur .
